item.title: NFL news, live updates: Aidan Hutchinson reportedly suffers torn ACL on sack celebration; Patriots QB Drake Maye out indefinitely with ankle injury
item.description: Follow along with the latest NFL news coming out of Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
Another NFL Sunday is in the books, with just one game left in Week 10 as the Baltimore Ravens host the LA Chargers on "Monday Night Football."

Sunday kicked off with a bang as the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots faced off in Munich, Germany, with injuries to two stars that will have all eyes drawn as the new week plays out. Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson suffered what is feared to be a season-ending ACL tear while celebrating a sack against Patriots quarterback Drake Maye … who suffered an ankle injury on that very sack, which knocked him out of the game and could cost him the season.

Week 10 also offered us our first look at Las Vegas Raiders No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza as a starter. He led scoring drives on each of the Raiders' first two possessions and entered halftime with a 10-7 lead over the Seattle Seahawks, but Drew Lock rallied with two passing touchdowns in the third quarter to take the lead, improving to 3-0 as a starter for Seattle this season. Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers exited the loss with an ankle injury.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 10.

item.title: Joe Burrow surges ahead of Josh Allen as NFL MVP favorite. 'Long season ahead,' he cautions
item.description: Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers to vault past Buffalo's Josh Allen to become the betting favorite for his first NFL MVP award.
item.content:encoded:
The fans in Cincinnati have spoken — Joe Burrow is the NFL’s MVP.

Sure, there are still two months of football to be played before those votes are cast, but the chants that rained down Sunday night at Paycor Stadium during the Bengals’ 38-18 dismantling of the Pittsburgh Steelers made it seem like a done deal.

“Finally,” Bengals receiver Ja’Marr Chasesaid of the MVP talk surrounding his QB. “He’s been deserving it. Finally getting the chants, too. About time.”

Cincinnati running back Chase Brown told reporters that the chants for Burrow were “well-deserved,” while coach Zac Taylor said that “people that aren’t talking about [Burrow] aren’t watching all of our games.”

Read more:Sean McVay showcases his ability to adapt in Rams’ blowout win over Cardinals

“Because if you are,” Taylor said, “it’s really hard to say that he’s not the best player on the planet Earth.”

Burrow’s performance on “Sunday Night Football” — during which he completed 35 of 44 passes (77.5%) for 409 yards, four touchdowns and a passer rating of 135.7 (his third-highest of the season) — seemed to convince folks outside of Cincinnati as well. The seventh-year player is now the betting favorite to win his first league MVP award, with FanDuel giving him 1-1 odds of claiming the honor.

Burrow now has scored four or more touchdowns in five straight games (he had five passing and one rushing during the Bengals’ 43-36 overtime win over the Tennessee Titans on Nov. 1). That ties an NFL record set by Peyton Manning in 2004, according to Pro Football Talk, and he won the second of his five league MVPs that year.

Read more:How Joe Burrow's hometown followed the quarterback into the 'Who Dey' army

The Bengals are 7-2 and in first place of the AFC North, with Burrow completing 74.7% of his passes for 2,795 yards with 27 touchdowns and six interceptions. He also has rushed for three touchdowns.

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen, who was tied with Burrow as the MVP favorites going into this weekend’s games, drops to No. 2 with 7-2 odds. The Bills are an AFC-best 8-1 behind Allen, who has completed 65% of his passes for 2,223 yards with 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He also has 11 rushing touchdowns.

Allen won the 2024 MVP award after completing 63.6% of his passes for 3,731 yards with 28 touchdowns and six interceptions.

Read more:Can the 0-8 Chargers finally win? Struggling Ravens provide an opportunity

Two other quarterbacks, San Francisco 49ers’ Brock Purdy and Jacksonville Jaguars’ Trevor Lawrence, appear to be in contention to win the award for the first time in their careers. Purdy (4-1 odds) has completed 70.1% of his passes for 2,369 yards with 20 touchdowns and five interceptions. Lawrence has completed 66% of his passes for 2,284 yards with 21 touchdowns and five interceptions.

Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes currently has the fifth-best chance to win his third MVP award, although his odds are significantly higher at 25-1. The two-time former MVP has completed 66.8% of his passes for 2,385 yards with 19 touchdowns and four interceptions.

Read more:Chargers vs. Baltimore Ravens: How to watch, start time, prediction and betting odds

While Burrow’s teammates think the MVP chants have been a long-time coming, the three-time Pro Bowl selection believes folks are getting ahead of themselves with such talk. Asked after the game what he thought about the chants, Burrow simply responded, “Long season ahead.”

Still, Burrow knows to give credit where it’s due. Asked what kind of quarterback he thought he was against the Steelers, he had another three-word answer.

“A great one,” Burrow said.

item.title: Replace Dominic Zvada? Do the NY Giants have any good options to do that?
item.description: There isn’t much to choose from on the kicker market.
item.content:encoded:
There is a vocal part of the New York Giants fan base that believes the team should have already booted rookie plackekicker Dominic Zvada to the curb. That is understandable. When something goes wrong, fans always want someone to blame, and invariably they want someone to lose a job so they feel like they got their pound of flesh.

The Giants have not been willing to do that as Zvada, after a 9-for-9 start, has made just 8 of 14 field-goal attempts over the past four games. Zvada has a much-discussed issue from the right hash mark.

“You can’t, as soon as a guy doesn’t make a play, start firing people left and right,” said head coach John Harbaugh.

It is always easy to say “that guy’s gotta go.” It is a lot tougher to look around and find a solution, to find someone you are certain is a better option.

Let’s look around and see what kind of options the Giants would have if they were to consider replacing Zvada.

Ben Sauls

The common refrain from Giants’ fans who want Zvada gone is, basically, “Better call Sauls.”

Left-footed Ben Sauls was an elixir for the Giants’ kicking woes at the end of the 2025 season. Sauls made all 15 of his kicks over a three-game span, eight field goals and seven extra points.

Yes, Sauls was perfect over that three-game stretch. Remember, though, his longest kick was a 45-yard extra point. Zvada has already been asked to try nine field goals of 50 yards or more, making six. Sauls has the leg for those kicks, but it’s never been tested in an NFL game.

It is also important to remember that Sauls, like Zvada is currently, went through his own technique issue in the spring and summer while competing with Zvada. He was terrible in the spring, consistently pushing kicks to the left. He was better in the summer, but wasn’t nearly as consistent kicking the ball as Zvada was.

It was easily to decide which of the two kickers should win the job.

Sauls is not currently on a 53-man roster or practice squad. To my knowledge, he may have only had one or two tryouts.

You can romanticize Sauls as the perfect solution to the placekicking issue if you want, but Sauls lost his job to Zvada because — based on the evidence at hand this summer — that is exactly what should have happened.

Zane Gonzalez

Gonzalez, 31, has had an up-and-down eight-year career. He made 19 of 22 field-goal attempts (86.4%) for the Atlanta Falcons in 2025. He got waived on Monday by the Miami Dolphins after he missed two field goals and an extra point in a 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts.

Gonzalez had replaced Riley Patterson earlier this season.

It’s hard to make a case that Gonzalez would be a better option that Zvada.

Old guys

The 42-year-old Matt Prater made 18 of 20 kicks (90%) for the Buffalo Bills last season. The last time he made less than 80% of his kicks in a season was 2020. He made a 57-yard kick for the Arizona Cardinals in 2024, so there should still be something left in his leg.

Are the Giants reaally in a situation where replacing Zvada with a guy almost 20 years older than he is would be the right move?

Graham Gano is also out there. And, he misses football.

Practice squad guys

Harrison Mevis is on the Baltimore Ravens’ practice squad. He went 5 of 9 for the Los Angeles Rams earlier this year.

Justin Tucker is with the Kansas City Chiefs. Once the best kicker in the game for Harbaugh’s Baltimore Ravens, Tucker made just 22 of 30 field goals (73.3%) in 2024. He served a supension in 2025 related to sexual misconduct allegations. Tucker turns 37 in a few days.

Final thoughts

Quite honestly, I don’t see any “no-brainer” decisions guaranteed to be better than working with Zvada and trying to get through his issue from the right hash mark.

item.title: Colts Monday Morning Awards: Week 10 vs. Dolphins
item.description: After a five-week winless drought that warranted a month-long hiatus from Monday Morning Awards, the Indianapolis Colts survived a late rally to hold off the Miami Dolphins in Sunday’s 24-22 win.
item.content:encoded:
After a five-week winless drought that warranted a month-long hiatus from Monday Morning Awards, the Indianapolis Colts survived a late rally to hold off the Miami Dolphins in Sunday’s 24-22 win. 

Here are the Monday Morning Awards from Sunday’s narrow victory.

MVP: Justin Walley

For the first time this season, there were at least three, four, maybe five players that had a case to be named the most valuable player of the game. When the offense looks as bad as it did in the second half, sometimes it takes the defense to put points on the scoreboard.

After rewatching the game, it’s definitive that without Walley’s takeaway to start the second half, the Colts do not escape with a win against the Dolphins. For a defense that has struggled to generate takeaways, Walley’s impact, timing and awareness earns him MVP honors. 

The second-year nickel collected five tackles, a critical sack, and etched career-highs with two pass deflections and two tackles for loss. Walley posted a 91.2 Pro Football Focus defensive grade in Week 10, which led all cornerbacks and was third among all NFL players on Sunday. He allowed just three catches on six targets for a minimal 13 receiving yards. Walley’s 22 defensive stops rank second among all cornerbacks this season.

Best Play of the Game: Justin Walley strip-sack, Adetomiwa Adebawore TD

On Miami’s first snap of the second half, cornerback Justin Walley came flying off the edge and strip-sacked quarterback Kyle McCord near the goal line. Defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore was in the right place at the perfect time to recover the fumble in the end zone for a defensive touchdown. The offense scored just three points in the second half, so this defensive score without a doubt gave the Colts enough cushion to not blow the lead. 

Adebawore is also having a phenomenal breakout season, posting an 84.3 pass rush grade that ranks second among defensive lineman, behind Cincinnati’s Dexter Lawrence. It’s fitting that Adebawore was ready for the opportunity to score as the football was knocked out of the grasp of McCord. Adebaware emerged as a full-time starter and has hit career highs with 11 QB hits, four sacks, and three pass deflections. Two weeks ago, Indianapolis signed the 25-year-old to a two-year, $35 million extension to lock in the centerpiece of their interior defensive front. 

Dud of the Game: Steichen & Jones co. 

Daniel Jones is off to the worst start of his career and is statistically the worst QB in the NFL. Jones threw two interceptions, including a pick-six on the very first play after the Dolphins had just cut into the deficit. He’s lucky his fumble rolled out of bounds before it had a chance to be recovered inside the red zone. It’s beyond irresponsible not to make a change. Jones has career-lows in completion rate (59%), yards per attempt (5.6), passer rating (67) and QBR (36.4). 

Shane Steichen needs to dramatically change the offense, sustain the run game and avoid passing to this batch of receivers until Alec Pierce returns to action. There’s no chance he didn’t hear the boos rain down during introductions, after the first fumble, or the five punts in the second half. The Dolphins also had five first downs gained because of a penalty, so I would be remiss to not add cornerback Kenneth Harris to the dud of the game. 

Worst play of the game: Daniel Jones pick-six

Despite taking a two-possession lead on the first play of the third quarter. Jones and Drew Ogletree both hand-wrapped a pick-six that allowed the Dolphins a chance to stay within striking distance. After Gonzalez finally connected on a field goal to cut the deficit to 21-10, the Colts next drive lasted for a single play. 

Jones instantly stumbled, but tried to scramble away to keep the play alive and forced a fadeaway throw, which ricocheted off the hands of Ogletree and was picked off by Dolphins cornerback Chris Johnson, who returned it for a 59-yard housecall. To be honest, it’s fair to say that the way Jones led the offense in the second half, dared the Dolphins to steal the win. 

Rookies of the week: C.J. Allen, Seth McGowan

Rookie running back Seth McGowan stacked another encouraging performance, rushing for a career-high 77 yards on 12 carries. McGowan punched in his second career touchdown from 4-yards out to give the Colts a lead they never relinquished. McGowan’s physicality and explosiveness gives the Colts a sledgehammer to lean on for the tough gains to get through battle. 

With Jonathan Taylor still leading the backfield tandem, McGowan is beginning to establish himself as a legitimate complementary piece. Taylor was the main name in headlines before the trade deadline, but the front office decided it was best to keep their star captain around for the rebuild. It was to McGowan’s joy of course, since he mentioned that he even prayed that Taylor would remain in Indy. The seventh-round draft pick has scored the first touchdown in each of the last two games, delivering both of his welcome to the league moments inside Lucas Oil Stadium. 

Perhaps it was rookie linebacker C.J. Allen who delivered the best overall performance on Sunday. More than one Stampede Blue writer seemed to think so. Allen made his presence felt with a game-high nine tackles and two tackles for loss. His biggest play came late in the fourth quarter when he sacked McCord for a 10-yard loss that speared the Dolphins out of field goal range. With Miami threatening to steal the game in the final minute, Allen was the green dot player who not only called the play, but was tasked to be the blitzer. The second-round draft pick has become a reliable presence in the middle of Lou Anarumo’s defense since earning the starting job. His instincts and physicality were put on full display in the critical final drive, which is difficult to ignore.

Unsung heroes: Spencer Shrader, A.J. Haulcy

When the Colts needed insurance, Spencer Shrader drilled a 51-yard field goal in the third quarter, extending the lead to 24-16. It ultimately proved to be the final points Indianapolis would score in a game that was decided by just two points. Shrader leads the league in made FGs of 50-plus yards, currently an efficient 9-for-10. He’s tied for the NFL lead with 88 total points this season and ranks second among kickers with 23 field goals made in 25 attempts (92%). 

With the offense unable to put the game away, Shrader’s long-distance connection became the deciding factor, especially when the Dolphins kicker left seven points off the scoreboard from two missed field goals and a missed extra point, all wide left. Multiple staff writers even comically discussed if Zane Gonzalez were the true MVP of the game. In a game decided by two points, every kick matters.

“No Fly Zone”: A.J. Haulcy

The Dolphins had a clear opportunity to level the score, but the young defensive pieces refused to let the lead slither away. After Miami scored a touchdown to cut the deficit to 24-22, rookie safety A.J. Haulcy broke up McCord’s two-point conversion attempt to preserve the lead. Even after Walley’s strip-sack and Adebawore’s fumble recovery touchdown proved to be the winning play, it was Haulcy’s rejection in the end zone that kept the Dolphins from making a full comeback. 

If anybody in the organization thinks this Monday is time to exhale, you are dead wrong. Five straight losses forced a trade-deadline fire sale, so the rest of the season is taken into the context that the white flag has already been waved to the rest of the NFL. It was stressful to watch the two-possession lead after the first play of the second half seemingly vanish, while trying to justify how this offense would be better off with Daniel Jones than any other QB on the roster moving forward.

After five consecutive defeats, the stampede sporting blue finally got to celebrate a win inside Lucas Oil Stadium. The offense moved the ball a combined 49 yards from where the seven second half possessions started. Jones had another multi-turnover outing, while the team committed 13 penalties and nearly lost against the worst tanking team in football. There are still plenty of reasons for concern, but the defense scored a touchdown, the running game went for 172 yards, and the young players made enough plays in the biggest moments to claim their third victory.

The Colts head to Houston, for a rivalry Thursday Night Football game against the Texans before reaching their BYE week.

item.title: Rams injuries from Week 10, Coleman Shelton exits early
item.description: The Rams suffered two more injuries along their offensive line in Week 10
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams dominated the Arizona Cardinals with a convincing 34-6 victory, but the win did not come without a few injuries – which has been typical for LA this year. Los Angeles suffered two significant injuries along the offensive line, a position that had been healthy for the first 8 1/2 weeks of the season. In a strange sequence of events, Los Angeles lost both centers during Sunday’s divisional matchup.

Coleman Shelton, C

Coleman Shelton was the first to go down, suffering a hamstring injury during the Rams’ second offensive series of the game. Shelton was initially considered doubtful to return before eventually being ruled out for the remainder of the afternoon.

Dylan McMahon, C

Unfortunately, his replacement didn’t last much longer. Backup center Dylan McMahon suffered a knee injury shortly after entering the game and was also ruled out. Suddenly, the Rams were without their top two options at center.

Sean McVay and the coaching staff responded by moving Beaux Limmer from left guard to center and inserting Bill Murray at left guard. The adjustments allowed the offense to continue operating without significant disruption.

The good news for Los Angeles is that the team now enters its Week 11 bye, providing additional time for both Shelton and McMahon to recover. With a challenging stretch of games approaching, getting healthy along the offensive line will be particularly important considering Steve Avila (hamstring) was injured in Week 9 and is expected to miss multiple weeks.

The Rams will need all hands on deck when they return to action against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, November 25.

item.title: Eagles roster news: Zach Ertz’s promotion among 7 moves
item.description: Philadelphia made some changes coming out of the bye.
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced seven transactions on Monday afternoon in the aftermath of their Week 10 bye. Here’s an overview:

  • TE Zach Ertz and OT John Ojukwu were signed from the practice squad to the active roster.
  • RB Will Shipley’s 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve was opened.
  • RB Jaydon Blue, LB Chance Campbell, and TE Hayden Rucci were signed to the practice squad.
  • DB Shaun Wade was released from the practice squad.

Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis.

ZACH ERTZ

We finally have resolution on the Eagles’ intentions for Ertz.

The team originally signed him to their practice squad after Dallas Goedert suffered an injury in Week 2. They then maxed out his three temporary elevations over the next three weeks. There was thought they’d sign the franchise legend to the roster after that … but they just … didn’t.

And so Ertz remained on the practice squad as the Eagles lost games to the Carolina Panthers, Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders, and New York Giants.

But now the 36-year-old (who celebrated his birthday on November 10) is eligible to suit up on game day again.

How much will Ertz actually play? That much remains to be seen. Goedert is still here. Johnny Mundt’s playing time has been going down, as it should. Honestly, there’s really no reason for him to still be on the roster. There’s really no need to play Grant Calcaterra on offense, either.

Meanwhile, the Eagles should be looking to find more snaps for Eli Stowers. The rookie tight end hasn’t done much to deserve them … but that much should be moot at this point in a lost season. If he’s going to struggle, so be it. It’s time to get him much-needed experience.

The most interesting angle on Ertz playing for the Eagles at this point is his pursuit of the franchise’s all-time receptions record, currently held by Harold Carmichael. Ertz is eight catches away from taking over sole possession of first place in that category. With eight games left to play, it’s more than doable.

I don’t know that force-feeding Ertz for the sake of breaking the record feels very fun. But it also wouldn’t have been fun to see him spending the rest of the year on the practice squad. Either let him play or cut him free. The Eagles chose the former.

JOHN OJUKWU

In case you missed it, the Eagles released Fred Johnson late last week. That move left them without a swing tackle on the roster.

Promoting Ojukwu gives the Birds depth behind Jordan Mailata and rookie Markel Bell. I don’t know that Ojukwu, who turns 28 in January, offers much in terms of long-term upside. But he does bring some experience to the table with nine starts over 16 career games played.

Not exactly surprising since Ojukwu has been with the Eagles longer but it is notable they went with him over former Giants first-round pick Evan Neal.

WILL SHIPLEY

The Eagles currently have one running back on their active roster: Saquon Barkley. And he’s been playing through multiple injuries.

It looks like Shipley will be returning from IR to give the Eagles more depth behind Barkley. He missed time after suffering “a partial tear of his plantar fascia.”

The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday, November 21 to activate Shipley in time to play in Philly’s Week 11 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

It’s worth noting that the Eagles did NOT open Tank Bigsby’s practice window to return from IR. He’s on track to miss at least one more game, if not multiple.

JAYDON BLUE

Blue has bounced between the Eagles’ practice squad and roster this season. The team has been reluctant to play the former Dallas Cowboys draft pick on offense (save for garbage time). He’s really only around as a break glass in case of emergency option. Plus, maybe the Eagles think he has some long-term potential.

CHANCE CAMPBELL

The Eagles previously terminate Campbell’s contract with an injury settlement after he went on the practice squad injured list in October. Now he’s back in Philly to potentially provide linebacker depth and help on special teams if called upon.

With Jihaad Campbell dealing with multiple injuries, the Eagles could look to use his two remaining temporary elevations for this season.

HAYDEN RUCCI

Rucci is a newcomer.

The Lititz, Pennsylvania native played college football at Wisconsin before entering the NFL as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2024. He’s since spent time with the Miami Dolphins, Detroit Lions, San Francisco 49ers, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Los Angeles Chargers.

With 144 offensive snaps and 104 special teams snaps played in 10 career games, Rucci has logged a single reception for seven yards.

Rucci gives the Eagles another body at tight end for practice purposes.

SHAUN WADE

Wade, 28, had two different stints on the Eagles’ practice squad this season after previously spending time with the team in training camp.

I know people probably don’t care much about who’s on the practice squad but I do think it makes sense to get younger there at this point in the season. As opposed to investing in more veteran players if the Eagles were actually good and competitive. The Eagles should be using their practice squad spots on younger guys with upside.

So long (again), Shaun Wade.

item.title: Seahawks ‘really optimistic’ Sam Darnold will return and start vs. 49ers
item.description: Let the bye week quarterback discussion begin in Seattle.
item.content:encoded:
After missing their last two games, Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold appears to be on track to return to practice next week, according to head coach Mike Macdonald.

The Seahawks starter has been out with quad and rib injuries he suffered against the Chicago Bears, his second injury stint of the 2026 season. Macdonald said on the Brock and Salk morning radio show that he’s “very optimistic” that Darnold could return to practice after the bye week and start for Seattle in their rematch against the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 29.

In his six full games, Darnold has thrown for 1,478 yards, 10 touchdowns and nine interceptions, while completing 60% of his passes. His completion percentage and success rate are his lowest since he was a starter for the Carolina Panthers back in 2021, leaving many with second thoughts about the quarterback that led the Seahawks to a Super Bowl last season.

It hasn’t helped that backup quarterback Drew Lock has steadied the ship, going 3-0 in his starts and topping the NFL in passer rating, while playing against some of the league’s worst defenses. For what it’s worth, Macdonald has steered clear of any quarterback controversy and repeatedly stood by Darnold through a turnover-filled rollercoaster season.

With the offense beginning to find rhythm in the run game and Jaxon Smith-Njigba putting up historic numbers, the situation Darnold returns to should be one better than when he left. The bye week should give the entire battered Seahawks time to heal, including tackle Charles Cross and guard Quenton Nelson, which would be massive for Darnold’s success down the stretch.

For now, the Seahawks will play the waiting game as they take a week off and see if they’ll get their starter back for a pivotal divisional showdown after Thanksgiving.

item.title: Emmett Johnson gets AP’s Game Ball from win over Falcons
item.description: Which player was Kansas City’s most important player in the win over Atlanta?
item.content:encoded:
The Kansas City Chiefs are 7-2 after a 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10.

Rookie running back Emmett Johnson took advantage of a rare opportunity to start and be the Chiefs’ bell-cow back for a day. He gained 171 yards from scrimmage, the fourth-most yards by a Chiefs player this year. Kenneth Walker has had games of 178, 179 and 191 yards this season.

It was Johnson’s breakout game into the national spotlight: NFL fans voting in SB Nation’s ‘Reacts’ poll on Sunday voted Johnson NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year at this point in the season.

On Monday, head coach Andy Reid was happy his first-year back got the recognition from the first 100-rushing-yard game of his career.

“We felt comfortable with that, that he could do that,” Reid told local media via video call. “He’s very capable, he’s got the right attitude, he has picked things up well, he’s a smart kid. We tried to get him that 100 yards, which we normally wouldn’t do, but he was so close, I thought it was a neat deal for him.”

Arrowhead Pride user saintschiefsfan compared Johnson’s running style to legendary running back Marcus Allen. That clicked with me; who does Johnson remind you of?

item.title: Vikings WR Jordan Addison needs thumb surgery, leaving Kirk Cousins without a top target for multiple weeks
item.description: Head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed the injury on Monday, telling reporters that Addison sustained a "freak" injury in practice last week.
item.content:encoded:
Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison has a thumb injury that requires surgery and will miss multiple weeks.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed the injury on Monday, telling reporters that Addison sustained a "freak" injury in practice last week. O'Connell did not reveal the precise nature of Addison's injury or how he sustained it.

Addison missed Sunday's win over the Green Bay Packers and may need a stint on injured reserve, which would require him to miss a minimum of four games.

The Vikings won Sunday's game in quarterback Kirk Cousins' first game back with the team since Minnesota traded for him last week from the Las Vegas Raiders. Cousins and the Vikings’ offense will now be down one of Minnesota's top weapons in the passing game.

Addison, 24, is the No. 2 receiver on Minnesota's depth chart behind four-time All-Pro Justin Jefferson. In seven games this season, Addison has 18 catches for 277 yards and 1 touchdown.

Like much of the rest of Minnesota's offense, Addison's production has dipped this season amid poor quarterback play from Carson Wentz and Kyler Murray that prompted the Vikings to trade for Cousins. Cousins provided an immediate boost to the Minnesota offense Sunday as the Vikings secured their 30-20 win over the Packers.

The Vikings broke a two-game losing streak and improved to 7-2 with the win. They're in a three-way tie with the Bears and Lions for first place in the NFC North.

The Vikings also played on Sunday without wide receiver Jauan Jennings (calf) and tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist, chest). The status for both moving forward isn't clear.

The Vikings will next take on the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers in a Sunday night showdown in Mexico City that has implications for the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoffs. They'll do so down at least one key player in the passing game.

item.title: Sean Payton: "There's no loophole" in the trade process
item.description: Payton disputes JIm Harbaugh's characterization of the failed Daiyan Henley trade.
item.content:encoded:
After last week's failed trade that would have sent Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Broncos, L.A. coach Jim Harbaugh said that the Broncos used a "loophole" to squeeze the Chargers into better terms before the deal imploded.

The Broncos had no comment last week, and coach Sean Payton hadn't spoken to reporters because Denver had a Week 10 bye.

On Monday, Payton was available to the media. And the first question asked what changed as to the Henley trade.

“Nothing changed," Payton said. "It was already stated. Everything was pretty clearly spelled out. I’m not going to get into the specifics. He’s a prospect we thought — and still do [think] — very highly of. It just didn’t work out and it’s not uncommon with trades. That’s kind of where it went, and I’ll leave it at that.”

So is there a loophole?

“There’s no loophole," Payton said. "It just is part of the trade process every step of the way.”

He's technically right, but there is a loophole. A team that has buyer's remorse can try to rely on issues with the physical to negotiate better terms. And an unscrupulous team could finalize a deal before the deadline with the plan of trying to improve the deal later, under the guise of a failed physical.

The easy fix, when it comes to deadline deals, is to take the position that, after the window for making trades closes, the player either passes the physical and the trade goes through as negotiated or the player fails the physical and the deal dies.

There should be no "maybe" box when it comes to physicals. Especially after the period for making trades has ended.

item.title: Colts injury update: Number of starters banged up headed into short week vs. Texans on TNF
item.description: A number of Colts starters are banged up headed into a short week versus the Texans on TNF
item.content:encoded:
Indianapolis Colts starting left tackle Bernhard Raimann has officially entered the league’s concussion protocol, after being evaluated and ultimately ruled out with a head injury during Sunday’s home win against the Miami Dolphins:

Raimann suffered the concussion during the first quarter and as mentioned, did not return. With the Colts already down starting right tackle Jalen Travis, backup Luke Tenuta came in at left tackle for Indianapolis—while routine starting right guard Matt Goncalves kicked out to right tackle to begin the game.

The 29-year-old Raimann has already suffered three medically documented concussions during his first five NFL seasons, so it is something to monitor going forward for the Colts medically and regarding Raimann’s continued playing career—as we saw former Colts Pro Bowl center (now retired) Ryan Kelly’s playing longevity cut a bit short later in his career because of re-occurring concussions.

Raimann had previously started all 10 games for the Colts so far this season.

Currently, Raimann is PFF’s 17th best graded offensive tackle with a +74.9 overall grade. In pass protection, he’s allowed 3.0 sacks, 3 QB hits, and 20 total QB pressures during his 356 total pass blocking snaps to-date.

Obviously, being down both starting offensive tackles potentially playing the Texans fearsome pass rush of Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter (albeit, who did miss Sunday’s game) off the edge doesn’t ideally bode well for Indianapolis’ offense and keeping Daniel Jones upright and pass pressure free in the pocket.

It’s worth noting that Colts starting cornerback Sauce Gardner left the game in the 3rd quarter due to a re-occurring calf injury and underwent an MRI after the game. It’s the third time since he was acquired last year from the New York Jets that he’s missed time because of the lingering calf injury.

Fellow starting cornerback Charvarius Ward also suffered a shin injury and was seen post-game walking around with a single crutch—meaning Indianapolis could be without both of its starting outside corners in a short-week headed in to face the Texans on the road for this week’s Thursday Night Football matchup.

item.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 11: Latest news, updates for Drake Maye, Kenneth Walker III, Brock Bowers, more players for fantasy football
item.description: We go over the Week 11 NFL Injury Report with latest news and updates, plus fantasy football analysis for key players.
item.content:encoded:
It was a rough week for the New England Patriots over in Germany. As we look over the Week 11 NFL injury report, the Patriots are going to pop up quite a bit going into their bye. We also have five other teams on bye — the Packers, Seahawks, Browns, Falcons and Rams. Those teams will hopefully get healthier over that span.

Below, we'll go over the latest injury news, providing updates on key players for fantasy football.

Quarterback

  • Drake Maye, NE (ankle) — Out indefinitely

  • Geno Smith, NYJ (concussion/ankle)

  • Sam Darnold, SEA (quad) — bye week

  • Baker Mayfield, TB (lower leg) — Could miss Week 11

Maye: New England heads into its bye, though the season may be lost coming out of it. At this point, it's feared Maye has a fractured ankle and could need season-ending surgery. At the very least, he could miss multiple games or be placed on IR. It's almost helpful that New England is on bye in Week 11, as fantasy managers would already be looking for a Maye replacement or streaming option.

If Maye is done for the season, it's difficult to trust anyone on this offense. There are injuries and ailments everywhere, from A.J. Brown to Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. The Pats are well behind the 8-1 Bills in the AFC East, though are still in the wild-card picture. But if Maye is out, that outlook could change fast. If you have any skill position player on New England, be sure to have contingency plans. This team could turn into a fantasy wasteland soon.

Mayfield: The Bucs are coming out of the Week 10 bye but may be without Mayfield. He suffered a lower leg injury in Week 9's loss to Chicago, and the extra rest didn't appear to help. If Mayfield is out against Detroit in Week 11, Jalon Daniels, who started three games earlier in the season, would get another shot. With so many teams on bye and Maye managers searching for answers, Daniels isn't a bad waiver add. Tampa Bay has a pretty soft schedule the rest of the season. Expect the Bucs to continue to ride the running game with Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell.

Running Back

  • Kenneth Walker III, KC (groin)

  • Woody Marks, HOU (concussion)

  • David Montgomery, HOU (groin)

  • Kyle Monangai, CHI (thumb/toe)

Walker: The Chiefs added Walker to the injury report last Friday and he was swiftly ruled out for Week 10 against the Falcons. As a result, rookie Emmett Johnson thrived in lead-back duties, totaling 171 yards on 28 touches (six catches) with two TDs for 32.1 fantasy points. Reports suggest this will be a short absence for Walker and he should be back Week 11 against the Cardinals.

If Walker is back, he should return to his role as the lead back and get the majority of the work. Johnson has played well enough to warrant touches, however, and could get extra work given the opponent. Kansas City is a heavy favorite in Week 11, and if the team pulls away, we could see Walker rest and Johnson get work in garbage time. If Walker is active, you're playing him, of course. But if you were able to snag Johnson off the wire, he's also in play as a flex option.

Texans RBs: Marks was forced to leave Week 10 against the Browns due to a concussion. He's unlikely to go Thursday against the Colts. Head coach DeMeco Ryans also doesn't know if Montgomery will be ready on the short week. If both backs are out, it's looking like Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale will split the work out of the backfield.

While it's a good matchup, if both Marks and Monty are out, neither depth back is a strong fantasy play. Each would be a risky flex option. Instead, expect the Texans to lean on the passing game, which has looked good over the past four games. Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte remain interesting adds off the waiver wire depending on league size/format.

We'll see what his practice status looks like but he'll need to clear protocol in order to play this week against the Saints. If Burden misses the game, it's a bump up for Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland in the pass game, while we may see more targets for Kalif Raymond.

Evans: The Niners may not be in a rush to get Evans back given the 46 points the offense scored on Sunday against the Cowboys. The veteran wideout missed his third straight game but will have a shot at returning in Week 11 against the Vikings, not an ideal spot. San Francisco also has a pretty crowded receiving room with Deebo Samuel Sr. returning and Keenan Allen coming over via trade, not to mention George Kittle and the emerging Jordan Watkins. They have signed tight end Zach Ertz and offensive tackle John Ojukwu to the active roster. They have also designated running back Will Shipley for return from injured reserve.

Ertz returned to the organization via the practice squad in September and was elevated to play in three games. He had three catches for 22 yards in those appearances.

Ojukwu has been on the practice squad since failing to make the team out of the summer, but has not appeared in any games. He played in 16 games for the Titans over the past three seasons.

Shipley had 20 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown in the first five games. He has missed the last four games with a foot injury.

item.title: NFC playoff picture: Rams still in the hunt
item.description: The Rams have moved up in the NFC standings but will need to finish the season strong to make the playoffs
item.content:encoded:
The NFC playoff picture is beginning to take shape, but the Los Angeles Rams are still on the outside looking in. Despite remaining firmly in the postseason hunt, the Rams currently sit ninth in the NFC standings, just outside the playoff picture with several teams competing for the conference’s remaining spots. Their latest win over the Arizona Cardinals certainly helps their postseason hopes, but there is still work to be done if Los Angeles wants to secure a playoff berth. With the NFC West race heating up and the conference standings continuing to shift, every remaining game carries significant weight. The Rams have positioned themselves to make a push, but they can no longer afford to let opportunities slip away.

Current NFC Standings…

#1 Seed: San Francisco 49ers (8-1)

San Francisco is going to finish with the NFC’s #1 seed. It’s just a matter of what week they lock it up.

#2 Seed: Detroit Lions (7-2)

The Detroit Lions may have moved up in the NFC standings over the last few weeks but now its come at the cost of Aidan Hutchison being out for the rest of the season due to a likely ACL tear via a sack celebration. Yikes…

I’m not sure the Lions are built to win track meets even despite having the easiest schedule in the NFL In all likelihood, Detroit finishes as the 6 or 7 seed.

#3 Seed: New York Giants (5-3-1)

By default. The NFC East is terrible.

#4 Seed: Carolina Panthers (4-5)

Also a division that no one wants to outright win – the NFC South. This week Carolina is in the poll position. Next week it will be?

#5 Seed: Minnesota Vikings (7-2)

The addition of Kirk Cousins will make the NFC North race interesting. The Vikings simply have to be mediocre on offense and they will guarantee themselves a playoff birth.

#6 Seed: Chicago Bears (7-2)

The Bears should finish as the #2 or #5 seed. They have a more complete team than Detroit.

#7 Seed: Green Bay Packers (6-4)

Green Bay has the tiebreaker over Seattle due to conference win percentage. Green Bay may be playing for its postseason life in Week 12 because a 5th NFC conference loss may be too tough to overcome.

#8 Seed: Seattle Seahawks (6-4)

Seattle has the tiebreaker over Los Angeles because of divisional record. Seattle has a bye in Week 11 but will have two weeks to prepare for the 49ers. A Seattle win could make the NFC West a three way race again.

But is this Sam Darnold’s team or Drew Lock’s?

#9 Seed: Los Angeles Rams (6-4)

The Rams are on the outside looking in right now. They have rattled off four straight wins (albeit against the Raiders, Chargers, Commanders, and Cardinals). A Week 11 bye comes at the right time as the team needs to get healthy for its last 7 games which features: Green Bay, Seattle (x2), San Francisco, Dallas, Tampa Bay, and Kansas City. All those games are against competition still in the playoff hunt, if not currently positioned to make the playoffs.

Another interesting note on the Rams is that they are 4-1 on the road this year. And that bodes well for the team as they will likely have to navigate 3 road playoff games if they want to play for Super Bowl LXI.

item.title: Who were the Titans’ 5 best players vs. Jaguars in Week 10?
item.description: Identifying the Tennessee Titans’ five best players from the Week 10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
The Tennessee Titans were defeated 40-23 by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 10. A familiar theme is emerging. The offense is beginning to show real signs of life while the defense flounders following the Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker trades.

Anyhow, we’ve identified and analyzed the Titans’ five best performances in Week 10.

QB Cam Ward

It was another strong performance for Titans quarterback Cam Ward. The sophomore No. 1 overall selection completed 28-of-39 passing attempts for 231 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception. He also rushed for a team-high 39 yards. Ward’s 28 completions tied a previous career high, and his 71.8% completion percentage was his best of the season.

LB Cedric Gray

Cedric Gray finally received an opportunity to play an every-down role with three linebackers sidelined by injury. Gray posted a team-high nine tackles, had two pass breakups, a TFL, and intercepted a tipped Trevow Lawrence pass. He better retain his starting role next weekend alongside Anthony Hill Jr. Cody Barton needs to be benched.

RT JC Latham

Right tackle JC Latham continues to take the desired steps forward. Pro Football Focus credited him with allowing two pressures and zero sacks. Latham has allowed two sacks all season long. He was downright dominant at times versus the Jaguars while providing Ward with clean pockets.

RB Tony Pollard

The Titans decided to retain Tony Pollard beyond the trade deadline despite having offers. He struggled to run the football effectively versus the Jaguars, being limited to 33 yards via nine carries. But Pollard made an outstanding individual effort on a 32-yard TD pass from Ward, and totaled 66 receiving yards on eight checkdowns.

WR Elic Ayomanor

With Carnell Tate sidelined, the supporting cast of receivers possessed an opportunity to shine. Though he wasn’t perfect, Elic Ayomanor was the offense’s leading receiver. Ayomanor posted five receptions for a team-high 79 yards, including an explosive 50-yard gain.

item.title: Jets coach Aaron Glenn reveals he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of Week 10 loss to Bills
item.description: Aaron Glenn took over defensive play calling in the offseason.
item.content:encoded:
New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn was hired by the team thanks to his excellence as a defensive coordinator. But after the team struggled on defense during Glenn's first year as head coach, he decided to take over defensive play-calling duties in 2026.

That change lasted just nine games. Glenn told reporters Monday he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of the team's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 10, per ESPN.

Glenn said the move was made to help the team win games. He added that while Jets defensive coordinator Brian Duker called plays Sunday, Glenn was "very involved" in the team's scheme.

"I've said this and I will continue to do this: Anything I can do as a head coach to help us win games, I'm willing to do it," Glenn said. "I'm not afraid to do that. So I gave him the lead, but I was very involved in what we ran."

The change appeared positive initially, as the Jets (2-8) gave up just 10 points in the first half Sunday. But Buffalo's offense got rolling the second half, allowing the team to pull away.

The Jets ultimately gave up 31 points in a loss to the Bills. Though, in Duker's defense, facing Josh Allen in your first game as a defensive play-caller is among the toughest asks in the NFL. The Bills rank first in the NFL with 31.9 points scored per game. In that sense, Duker's defense actually held the team under its season-long average … barely. The Jets still allowed 31 points, so the team shouldn't start popping the champagne just yet.

Glenn was noncommittal on whether Duker would continue to call defensive plays for the Jets, per ESPN. It was the first time ever in Duker's career that he was tasked with calling plays in a game. The 37-year-old has spent time as an assistant and position coach during his career, but this is his first season as an NFL defensive coordinator.

The decision puts Glenn in a tough spot with seven games left in the regular season. Since being hired, Glenn is just 5-22 with the Jets. The team has shown some improvement on both offense and defense in 2026, but not enough to drastically alter its outlook. Unless that improvement starts leading to wins down the stretch, Glenn could be out of a job at the end of the year.

item.title: 10 Eagles things I think I think coming out of the bye week
item.description: Thoughts about the Eagles as they didn’t play this week.
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Eagles didn’t lose this week — because they didn’t play.

The bye week is normally a time for players to regroup and get healthy. There are a lot of players the Eagles could use back, but this is a team that’s 2-7 with their season a lost cause. They haven’t won a game since September 20, a good two months once Philadelphia returns to action against the Pittsburgh Steelers on November 22.

This was a good week to get away from the Eagles, but there are still eight more games to be played in his dismal season. A lot happened during the bye week, with the Eagles and around the NFL (there never seems to be a shortage of storylines in this league).

As the Eagles bye week came and went, here were a few things I noticed watching the NFL this weekend — and other sports.

1. The NFC East isn’t good — again

Every year this seems to be a thing, even when the Eagles have a Super Bowl contending team. Outside of 2022 and 2024, there isn’t much to brag about when it comes to watching the football teams play in the NFC East.

The Washington Commanders win over the New York Giants on Thursday night was a rough watch, but playing on a short week didn’t help either of those teams either. I also wasn’t impressed with the Giants’ win over the Eagles in Week 9, wondering how New York was ahead of the Dallas Cowboys in the division.

Then, the Cowboys gave up 584 yards and 9.4 yards per play to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. This comes a week after surviving against the Indianapolis Colts — who might be as bad as the Eagles.

The NFC East has a combined record of 14-21-2 — a .405 win percentage. The four NFC East teams are 7-14 against opponents not in the division — a .333 win percentage.

Who wins the NFC East is anyone’s guess (it won’t be the Eagles), but that division champion has the look of a one-and-done team in the playoffs. Dallas should be the best team in this division, but can’t get out of its own way.

2. The Sixers have taken over this city

I spent the bye week going to see the Philadelphia Sixers on Sunday afternoon, and it’s incredible how the vibes changed with this team over the last five months.

Even though the Sixers finally beat the Boston Celtics in the playoffs last year, that team wasn’t going to win the championship as they were constructed. Mike Gansey changed the direction of this franchise in a month, getting Jaylen Brown followed by LeBron James in the blockbuster moves of the offseason.

Xfinity Mobile Arena was buzzing towards that team on Sunday, with every LeBron pass and brown shot. Not to mention Tyrese Maxey is one of the best scorers in the league and V.J. Edgecombe is a blossoming star.

The building erupted when Maxey lobbed an alley-oop to James, and had me reminiscing of how much fun that 2000-2001 team was that won the Eastern Conference.

The Sixers are everything the Eagles aren’t right now. They have a lot of stars that are performing at a high level and they’re fun to watch. They also win games, as their 11-3 record is second in the Eastern Conference, and their best start since 2000-2001.

With the Eagles season a lost cause, the Flyers being the Flyers, and the Phillies getting older, the Sixers are the only hope in Philadelphia for a championship in the coming months. This city used to have that vibe for the Eagles…

3. Why I think Nick Sirianni won’t be back

Watching a few NFL games this weekend (and keep in mind I covered the league for a decade), other teams just are more exciting to watch than the Eagles. The San Francisco 49ers have an aging roster of skill players and create explosive plays on the regular.

The Cincinnati Bengals and Detroit Lions are the same way, even though those teams have their flaws. The Los Angeles Rams don’t have Davonte Adams and Puka Nacua and the offense don’t seem to miss a beat.

Why can’t the Eagles get anything going on offense? This lies deeper than the team being on the QB5 and WR3 and WR4 as the starters as recently as last game. This offense was a problem last year when the Eagles had their skill players healthy and had the most expensive offense in the NFL.

The Eagles are only 20th in cash spending on offense (currently), but this unit is last in yards per game (260.4), yards per play (4.3), and 30th in offensive points per game (16.4). They lead the league in three-and-out percentage (42.9%) and are last in 20+ yard play percentage (3.5%). The Eagles are also 25th in explosive play rate (9.3%).

Sirianni has an offensive background, yet the Eagles offense gets worse every year — no matter the play caller. On top of the seven-game losing streak and his inability to fix what’s broken, the NFL may have evolved past Sirianni.

The Eagles may have to change things up to keep up with the current NFL. Other teams are playing offense at a way different level than the Eagles.

4. Eagles won the A.J. Brown trade

Brown had degenerative knee issues during his time with the Eagles, and his production was slowly decreasing over the last few years in Philadelphia. brown’s best years were with the Eagles, but he still had some good years in him once he was traded to the New England Patriots right?

The first year in New England has been a disaster — for Brown and the Patriots. Brown has 11 catches for 128 yards and 0 TD in four games, having three drops and battling numerous injuries to his ankle, knee, and hamstring.

Brown is averaging career-lows in yards per catch (11.6), yards after catch per reception (3.4), receptions per route (10.6%), receptions per target (42.3%), yards per route run (1.23), yards per target (4.92), and drop rate (12.0%). The Patriots gave up a 2028 first-round pick for this.

Give credit to Eagles general manager Howie Roseman. He had no other suitors for Brown and had to wait until the June 1-deadline to even deal Brown due to his contract and all the dead money tied into it. Roseman still got a first-round pick for Brown, not worrying about the year of the pick — but the value of it.

Brown can still turn things around in 2027, but his best football was clearly with the Eagles. The Patriots paid for past production.

5. Speaking of the WR1

DeVonta Smith has been out since Week 6 with a hamstring injury. He’s only played in four games this season, totaling 26 catches for 310 yards and 2 TD, averaging a career-high 77.5 yards per game.

The Eagles really haven’t gotten to see Smith perform as the WR1 since he’s been battling this hamstring injury all season, and Smith only caught passes from Jalen Hurts for three games. He only played one game with Tanner McKee before the injury cost him the last three games.

Hopefully the hamstring injury is past Smith and he’s back following the bye. The same goes for Dontayvion Wicks and his injury, as the Eagles need both wide receivers to have a pulse on offense.

The offense is hurting Smith’s production too. He’s averaging career-lows in yards per catch (11.9), yards after catch per reception (1.8), yards per target (7.56), explosive play rate per target (17.1%). The good news? Smith has a career-high in yards per route run (2.26).

Hopefully Smith can made the most out of this year, or at least help out whoever plays quarterback.

6. No more Hollywood Brown or Fred Johnson

The Eagles released Hollywood Brown and Fred Johnson during the bye week, cutting ties with a wide receiver who couldn’t see the field and a swing tackle who wasn’t playing over rookie Markel Bell.

Philadelphia signed Brown to a $5 million deal, and he had five catches for 63 yards in four games — or $1 million per catch. Brown couldn’t get on the field over Makai Lemon (even when he was struggling) or Darius Cooper, so there was no need to keep him around on a 2-7 team.

Johnson’s release is interesting, as he’s likely a more competent option at right tackle than Bell right now. The Eagles have to play Bell the rest of the year, but Bell also has no veteran to push him in practice. Johnson may have given Bell the opportunity to reset before he takes the field again.

The Eagles also only have three tackles on the roster — Jordan Mailata, Markel Bell, and Lane Johnson (and Lane Johnson is retired). So they really only have two tackles available.

Someone is getting signed or called up from the practice squad. John Ojukwu or Kiran Amegadjie are the candidates there, and both deserve an extended look anyway. A move has to be made at tackle this week if the Eagles are just riding with Bell at right tackle.

7. Cole Payton starts a game this year

The 2026 Eagles just have the vibe of the 1998 Eagles, a team that just rotated quarterbacks throughout the year. The only difference is the 2026 Eagles had a franchise quarterback that was lost for the year, so they’re scrambling to pick up the pieces.

Tanner McKee wasn’t good enough in his three starts, so Joe Milton is getting an extended look. The Eagles will likely start Milton more than three games, but if Milton doesn’t play well in December — the front office and coaching staff will have to try something else.

This is where Payton comes in, as the Eagles will want to see how their fifth-round developmental quarterback looks at some point in a lost year. Maybe Payton is good enough to be the QB2 on this team. That’s what the Eagles are trying to find out with Milton right now.

Whether it’s in December or January, it’s likely Payton starts a game at quarterback. Whenever he’s ready.

8. About Jalen Hurts

I really don’t know if Hurts can play football again, since the Eagles aren’t giving any updates on his condition. Howie Roseman won’t even have a post-trade deadline press conference to avoid any questions asked about Hurts.

The hope is Hurts is back as the Eagles quarterback for 2027, but his future playing football is uncertain right now. That’s the reality the Eagles are facing.

The Eagles are in position for a top-5 pick right now. Do they use that pick to get a quarterback? Package the Jacksonville Jaguars’ first-round pick to move up and get a quarterback they like — and develop for the future?

There’s so much at play right now. If Nick Sirianni isn’t back, the new head coach may want a different quarterback. Hurts may not be able to play football again, or Hurts returns and the Eagles keep things status quo.

There’s too much with Hurts’ situation that needs to be unraveled. Wish the Eagles would give an update on how he’s doing, but alas. Things are business as usual there, when it shouldn’t be.

9. Eli Stowers should see more snaps — even if he hasn’t earned them

Since the 2026 Eagles season is a lost cause, the team should be giving their rookies more snaps. Makai Lemon has gotten those opportunities due to injuries at wide receiver, and had some highs and lows over the last three weeks. Markel Bell has struggled at right tackle, but the Eagles released Fred Johnson and eliminated any veteran competition there.

The Eagles haven’t done that at tight end. Grant Calcaterra and Johnny Mundt are still with the team, playing over second-round pick Eli Stowers for TE2 snaps. Stowers still struggled with his blocking and injuries held him back at the start of the year, but he’s healthy now and needs live reps.

Is there really a reason to play Mundt and Calcaterra when the duo give the Eagles nothing in the passing game? Why not see if Stowers can handle himself against NFL defenders, and if he can improve each week?

Stowers hasn’t really earned those snaps yet, but this season has shifted to developing players. That includes Stowers, who should be getting more snaps with Lemon and Bell the rest of the way.

The Eagles need to see if Stowers can play. This is the ideal opportunity, especially since Mundt and Calcaterra likely won’t be on this team next year.

10. It’s time to pay Moro Ojomo

Since the Eagles traded Jordan Davis — and got a 2027 first-round pick and 2029 second-round pick in return — that freed up the front office to pay Ojomo at some point this year.

Once the Eagles signed Jalen Carter, re-signing Ojomo seemed like a pipe dream. Carter and Davis were both amongst the highest-paid players at their position, and there was no way the Eagles had the cap space at defensive tackle to pay three of them.

The Eagles don’t need a nose tackle if Vic Fangio retires, as Ojomo would be a better fit for whatever defense they run. Ojomo will also get an opportunity for more snaps the rest of the way in 2026.

Ojomo’s numbers aren’t great this year, as he doesn’t have a sack and his pressure rate is down from 11.6% to 9.6%. He still has 21 pressures and five quarterback hits, and should be more productive with more snaps.

The Eagles pass rush has been underwhelming across the board, but Ojomo should have a strong finish to the season. If not, the Eagles may be able to sign him cheaper than his going rate at the beginning of the year — especially if they can get an extension done early.

Bonus: Shoutout to the Pope John Paul II football team. I’m an assistant coach for PJP (Royersford, Pa.) and just completed my first season on the staff. We finished 9-3 and fell to Pottsgrove in the District 1-AAAA title game Friday night, ending an impressive season.

I had a lot of fun helping out this team this year and we had a great group of seniors. There’s something so fulfilling in coaching, even though we didn’t meet our goal (it’s hard to win championships). 9-3 is a successful year (8-2 in regular season) and the players should have plenty to be proud of, even if the loss hurts right now.

Wish the seniors the best of luck going forward. Great group to work with, as was the rest of the team. Can’t wait for year two.

item.title: Steelers' veteran CB was torched by Joe Burrow in loss to Bengals: PFF grades
item.description: It was a bad night for the Steelers’ secondary as a whole, but no one was torched individually by Joe Burrow quite like one veteran CB.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers were blown out by a 38-18 margin in their crucial AFC North showdown with the Cincinnati Bengals on Nov. 15. 

At 6-3, they’re now a game back in the division and may be forced to play catch up the rest of the way if they hope to host a playoff game at Acrisure Stadium come January. 

Here’s a look at some of the highlights and (mostly) lowlights through the lens of Pro Football Focus evaluators, who study every play on film to grade each player individually on a 0-100 scale.

Required reading: NBC's Mike Tomlin gives blunt assessment of Steelers' loss to Bengals

Germie Bernard (49.2) 

Since his game-winning touchdown catch in Week 6 against Tampa Bay, opposing defenses have largely taken the rookie receiver out of the game. He has just eight catches for 57 yards, an average 7.1 yards per reception. Against the Bengals, he caught none of his three targets and was blanked for the first time since the season opener against Atlanta. This lack of production unfolds against the backdrop of major injuries at the position. Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson have been out for several weeks, so the pressure has been on Bernard to step up to try to draw some coverage away from DK Metcalf. The fact that he hasn’t meaningfully done that for several weeks is a concerning sign and adds to the urgency to get Pittman and Wilson back into the lineup as soon as possible. 

Asante Samuel Jr. (34.3) 

It was a bad night for the Steelers’ secondary as a whole, but no one was torched individually by Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins quite as bad as their veteran cornerback. Samuel was targeted seven times and allowed a whopping 135 of Burrow’s 409 yards in the contest on five receptions. That translates to a disastrous average of 27.0 yards per catch allowed. The Steelers’ soft zone has done a nice job keeping the proverbial lid on opposing offenses this season and avoiding big plays. Samuel has played a big part in that. But against a division rival with the most potent passing game in football right now, he made fans wish general manager Omar Khan had simply paid up to sign Joey Porter Jr. long-term at the position, particularly when Burrow targeted rookie teammate Daylen Everette just once on 17 coverage snaps. he Bengals clearly saw Samuel as the weak link and were proven correct. That’s a concerning development to watch in the second half of the season. 

Brock Hoffman (60.0)

The veteran right guard has received a lot of credit in recent weeks for changing the trajectory of the offensive line alongside rookie right tackle Max Iheanachor since both were added to the starting lineup in Week 3. PFF evaluators haven’t been impressed with him individually for several weeks, though. The game at Cincinnati marked the fourth time in the past five games that Hoffman has scored 62.3 or worse. He’s allowed 10 pressures in that span and has three run blocking scores at 51.2 or worse. Iheanachor is the team’s 2026 first-round pick, so coach Mike McCarthy will be hesitant to mess with his development, even if and when he struggles at time. Hoffman, on the other hand, needs to be better to justify a spot in this lineup. Especially now that left tackle Mason McCormick may be dealing with a serious injury on the opposite side.

Patrick Queen (81.5)

This was one of those games when you expected to open up the PFF scores on Monday morning and see some ugly ones for the inconsistent veteran linebacker, just because Burrow was able to have so much success against his defense generally. When the defense plays poorly, traditionally it follows that Queen did as well. Not this time. He allowed receptions on all six occasions when Burrow targeted him, but those plays went for just a total of 30 yards, or five yards per reception allowed. Importantly, he did a nice job smothering plays when they came to him. He totaled 10 solo tackles without a miss on the evening. He also tied a season high with five stops, defined by PFF as plays that result in failure for the opposing offense. This was the third consecutive game where he was graded at 75.6 or higher, so he really seems to be finding his way in this Patrick Graham scheme in a way he never quite did under former coach Mike Tomlin.
